notes.trap: An unsupported bitLength (anything other than 0, 224, 256, 384 or 512) returns NULL instead of raising an error, even with ANSI off. A typo such as 265 therefore silently yields NULL hashes.

`hash(...)` is a 32-bit signed Murmur3 hash, so the result is type-sensitive: the same numeric value hashes differently as INT and as BIGINT. NULL arguments are skipped rather than making the result NULL.
NULL inputs do not produce NULL. They are skipped, so an all-NULL argument list returns the seed value 42. NULL keys therefore all collide on 42 rather than being filtered out.
Unlike `hash(...)`, which returns a possibly negative INT, `crc32(...)` returns the unsigned CRC-32 value widened to BIGINT, so it is never negative.
